rationale: Both oil groups followed a ketogenic diet. Table 2 compares overall mood disturbance. The day-specific results are mixed and a separate depression estimate is unavailable.
Sunflower oil is the long-chain comparator. Overall mood results vary and anxiety is unavailable as a separate estimate. The refining grade and Parkinson population are unverified for this exposure.
The original analyzes the keto-induction symptom sum and the total mood-disturbance score. A separately estimated fatigue outcome or high-oleic sunflower preparation is unavailable.

Quinoa fiber was tested on donated fecal samples in a fermentation assay. The 24 Parkinson and 39 control donors did not receive a quinoa intervention. The experiment reported metabolites and no rigidity or other symptom change.

Twelve participants reported daily olive oil and 45 reported constipation. The published table stratifies by underweight status rather than olive-oil intake, so there is no measured exposure-outcome contrast.
Daily olive oil is a questionnaire item. The paper gives no anxiety estimate linked to olive oil and no confirmation of cold-pressed preparation.
